springBatch.title: Spring Batch Chunk Engine & Skip/Retry Policies
springBatch.subtitle: Visualize ItemReader → ItemProcessor → ItemWriter chunk commit boundaries, backoff retries, and skip limits.
springBatch.mentalModel: Spring Batch reads items one by one into a chunk buffer — when chunk size (e.g. 5) is met, all items write in a single DB transaction.

failureModes: Corrupt Data Rollback Cascade: Without a SkipPolicy, a single invalid record in a 1,000,000-item job causes transaction rollback and kills the entire batch execution.
tradeOffs: Chunk Size 10 vs 1000: Smaller chunk size minimizes rollback data churn on errors but increases DB transaction overhead. Larger chunk size maximizes write throughput at higher memory footprint.
theoryData.productionScenario: A nightly financial settlement job processing 5M records crashed midway every night due to bad customer records. Adding `skip(CorruptDataException.class)` with `skipLimit(100)` allowed the job to finish in 8 minutes while logging bad records into an audit skip table.

interviewQA.q: What happens when an exception occurs inside ItemProcessor during a chunk commit?
interviewQA.a: Spring Batch rolls back the active transaction for the entire chunk. If a Skip Policy is configured, it re-reads the items one-by-one in non-chunked mode to isolate the single bad item, skips it, logs it to `BATCH_STEP_EXECUTION`, and resumes chunked processing.

quizData.question: If chunk size is 100 and item 47 throws a skipped exception, how many items are committed in the database?
quizData.answer: Item 47 is skipped. The remaining 99 valid items in that chunk are processed and committed together in the transaction.
